elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New 10.9: "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall exceed..." — the cap runs to both Parties, not Vendor only.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000)" — correct basis (fees, not all amounts), correct temporal anchor (preceding the claim) and correct floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "and neither Party shall be liable for any indirect or consequential damages" — bilateral by its terms.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations, and the cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include breach of "data protection or security obligations".

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: "The Company's obligations to pay amounts due under this Agreement shall not be considered damages subject to such cap." The Company is the Customer alias and the carve-out covers all amounts due, not a narrow defined subset of Fees; the deterministic check flagged this only because the drafted wording differs lexically from the model phrase.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "neither Party's total aggregate liability ... shall exceed" — mutual.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap floor is "the fees paid or payable by the Company ... in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim".
Excluded Claims include indemnification obligations and sit outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include breach of confidentiality obligations.

reasons: The finding of 'missing' is supported: the cited sections (9 Warranties, 10 General Provisions through 10.8 Headings; Counterparts) contain no cap, no exclusion of damages and no aggregate-liability language, so a concise insertion is the appropriate remedy.

New Section 10.9 is a single self-contained insertion that tracks the playbook model language and reaches every preferred element; all its words are new, which is acceptable for a missing clause, and no existing favourable language was deleted or paraphrased.

The deterministic check 'preferred payment carve-out covers Customer payment obligations' returns false, but on substance the sentence excludes the Company's obligations to pay all amounts due under the Agreement — the whole payment obligation rather than a narrowly defined subset of Fees — so the element is met despite the lexical mismatch.

No extras were added: there is no separate survival tail, no additional damages categories, no procedures or boilerplate; survival is left to existing Section 10.7 and mentioned only in the margin comment, not in operative text.

'Excluded Claims' is defined within the inserted section, so no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and no retained sentence contradicts the new cap or the mutual consequential-damages exclusion.
